the model says the meaning changed: The ask gate now stops applying in an attended session whenever the transcript shows a ToolSearch for "question" that did not return AskUserQuestion, so edits and writing shell commands are no longer refused while questions are open, which weakens EX-6 and the "asked as soon as raised" rule, and the requirement does not list this exception.; brought to the owner as a card: The requirement still matches what you asked for. You want every question from the judge to reach you as soon as it comes up. Until the agent asks the open questions, the ask gate blocks it from editing files or running shell commands that write (example EX-6).

The change adds a case where the gate turns itself off. If the agent used its tool search to look for the question tool and no search found it, the session is treated as having no question tool, so the agent can keep editing. The code points to a test run where the tool really was missing. In that case the gate would block the agent with no way to unblock, so the change looks like a fix for a real deadlock. The requirement doesn't mention this case, though, and EX-6 says writes are refused in any session you attend.

Three things are unclear:
- There's no logged message from you behind the change, so it may not be something you asked for.
- The check is loose. Any tool search with the word "question" in it counts, so a search for something else can switch the gate off even when the question tool exists.
- Once the gate is off, open questions just wait. That goes against "nothing is kept for a later turn."; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change, and add to the requirement that the gate stands aside only when the question tool is truly missing in the session.") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the idea but make the check tighter, so a search for the question tool itself has to fail before the gate stands aside.") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the change: the gate always holds in a session you attend, and a missing tool is handled some other way.") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (iaso stale card SR-361#5 --consequences "..." --why "...")
